correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization gives the exact radial kernels and antipodal polynomial; Walsh-coordinate splitting gives marginal and strict radial-difference identities. A probability variance obstruction and explicit d=2,3 inequalities bound the derivative alternating-series ratios strictly below one at every relevant time. Induction proves a single sharp crossing after the previous dimension recovers, precise boundary and universal monotone thresholds. The log(d)/4 bracket and j>=3 O(d^-6) remainder yield the three-term asymptotic. Standard-library checker passed 1936 exact-rational and high-precision finite consistency checks; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: Maximum-norm and order-preserving stability of a biharmonic smoothing semigroup is a meaningful sharp endpoint invariant. The theorem completely classifies the positivity-time set for every Boolean cube (not just an eventual bound), proves its antipodal controlling geometry, exhibits strict dimensional monotonicity, and derives a nontrivial logarithmic recovery scale and two finite-dimension correction orders; these conclusions are not routine consequences of general eventual positivity theorems.
